core_obligations: The class of pairs (proof lines 9562-9577): the author introduces the set of pairs consisting of a finite covering and an element of the value of the functor, and considers refinements of the given system satisfying the two required properties, ordered by inclusion and refinement; the class is shown to satisfy the hypotheses of Zorn's lemma for totally ordered subsets.

Zorn applied to the class (proof lines 9578-9593): for a totally ordered subset the union is again an element of the class, because the two sections remain distinct in the colimit over the union by the description of directed colimits of sets.

The transfinite construction (proof lines 9595-9614): since the class need not be a set, the author instead well orders the set of pairs and constructs, by transfinite recursion, a compatible family of refinements, refining at each step with respect to the corresponding pair using the one-step lemma, and takes the union.
proof_roadmap: Introduce the class of refinements satisfying the two required properties.
Check the hypotheses of Zorn's lemma for totally ordered subsets using directed colimits of sets.
Replace the appeal to Zorn by a transfinite recursion along a well ordering and take the union.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a system can be refined so that two distinct sections remain distinct and every element of the value of the functor becomes liftable through a member of any prescribed finite covering (statement lines 9546-9559). The proof is a complete argument: the author introduces the class of refinements satisfying the two properties and verifies the hypotheses of Zorn's lemma for totally ordered subsets, using the description of the values of the functor as directed colimits of sets (proof lines 9562-9593); because the class need not be a set, the appeal to Zorn is replaced by a transfinite recursion along a well ordering of the set of pairs, each step using the one-step refinement lemma, and the union of the resulting systems gives the solution (proof lines 9595-9614). The non-formal content is the passage from the Zorn argument to the transfinite construction. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
